title: Google Search Engine: Complete Architecture
description: Design a web search engine at Google scale with distributed crawling, inverted indexing, PageRank, scatter-gather query serving, and ML ranking.

data.text: Design a global web-scale search engine like Google. The system crawls billions of web pages across the public internet, parses and extracts document text and hyperlinks, creates and maintains a compressed inverted index, and serves user search queries with relevance ranking in sub-200ms at hundreds of thousands of queries per second (QPS).

terms.definition: A data structure mapping every distinct word/term to a posting list containing Document IDs, term frequencies, and word positions.
An iterative link-analysis algorithm that assigns numerical weights to hyperlinked documents based on the authority of incoming links.
A distributed query technique where a root node broadcasts a search query to hundreds of index leaf shards in parallel, merging and re-ranking the top results.
Locality-sensitive hashing algorithms used during crawling to detect near-duplicate web documents and save indexing capacity.
Techniques like Delta-encoding + Varint (VByte) to compress billions of DocIDs into compact memory-mapped index blocks.

data.title: Functional Requirements
items: Continuous Crawling: Discover and fetch billions of web pages while obeying robots.txt and host politeness rules
Document Parsing & Dedup: Strip HTML tags, extract text, compute document fingerprints (SimHash), and discard duplicates
Inverted Index Creation: Build forward indices and invert them into compressed posting lists with term positions
Search Query Processing: Parse query terms, handle operators (quotes, AND, OR, site:), expand synonyms, and spell-correct
Relevance Ranking: Score matching documents combining BM25, PageRank authority, freshness, and ML neural re-ranking
Snippet & Highlighting: Extract relevant sentences containing matching keywords for the search result page (SERP)

data.title: Non-Functional Requirements
items: Scale: Index 50+ billion web pages; serve 100,000+ queries per second (QPS)
Latency: Strict sub-200ms P99 search response time globally
Availability: 99.999% uptime for the query serving tier
Index Freshness: News and trending content re-crawled and indexed in minutes; static pages updated within days
Fault Tolerance: Sharded index leaf nodes must support automatic replica failover without dropped queries

data.text: The search engine system splits into two distinct, decoupled subsystems: the Offline Pipeline (Web Crawler, Inverted Index Builder, PageRank Calculator) and the Online Query Serving System (Query Parser, Scatter-Gather Index Searchers, ML Ranking Engine, and Snippet Generator).

data.text: To achieve sub-200ms latency across billions of indexed pages, the search query is broadcast simultaneously to all index shards. Each leaf node evaluates matching posting lists in memory and returns its local top-K candidates to the aggregator.

faqs.question: How is the inverted index partitioned: Document Sharding vs Term Sharding?
faqs.answer: Google uses Document Sharding (Local Inverted Index). Each shard contains the complete dictionary for a subset of all documents. When querying, the request is broadcast to all shards (scatter-gather). This prevents single-term hotspots (like the word "the" or "weather") from overwhelming one server, and keeps shard failures isolated.

faqs.question: How are posting lists compressed to fit in memory?
faqs.answer: DocIDs in a posting list are strictly ascending. Instead of storing 64-bit integers [1000, 1005, 1012], we store delta differences [1000, 5, 7]. Small numbers require only 1 or 2 bytes using Variable Byte (Varint) or Elias-Fano encoding, reducing index size by over 85%.

faqs.question: How is index freshness balanced with high search throughput?
faqs.answer: Use a tiered indexing model: a Real-Time Index (in-memory LSM-tree) updates breaking news within seconds, while the Base Master Index (tens of billions of pages) is re-indexed daily or weekly via distributed batch pipelines. Query aggregators search both tiers and merge results seamlessly.

faqs.question: How does Google handle tail queries and spelling mistakes?
faqs.answer: Query understanding applies spelling correction via character-level language models and n-gram dictionaries. Synonyms are expanded using embedding vector distance. If a query yields zero hits, relaxed term matching (dropping non-essential words) is automatically evaluated.

faqs.question: What happens if 2 out of 500 leaf shards timeout during scatter-gather?
faqs.answer: Strict SLA enforcement: if a shard does not respond within 80ms, the aggregator proceeds with results from the other 498 shards rather than blocking the user. Users would rather see 99.6% complete results in 120ms than wait 5 seconds for 100% completeness.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Document partitioning (scatter-gather) distributes query loads evenly without hotspot terms
Inverted indices store delta-compressed posting lists with term positions for fast phrase search
Two-tier ranking separates cheap candidate retrieval (BM25 + PageRank) from deep ML neural scoring
Tiered indexing (real-time in-memory + master batch) provides both instant freshness and petabyte scale
Aggregator timeouts gracefully degrade search completeness to safeguard sub-200ms P99 latency
data.takeaway: Search engine scalability relies on document-partitioned inverted indices queried via scatter-gather. Strict tail latency management and multi-stage ranking deliver relevant results from 50 billion pages in a fraction of a second.
